HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P)

History:
• Presenting complaint: Right-sided knee pain with clicking and episodic tingling in right toes  
• Onset/progression: Began ~2 weeks ago after increasing running mileage (training for June marathon). Pain starts ~20 minutes/≈mile 3 into a run, has progressively worsened to the point she stops running.  
• Characteristics: Achy pain felt mainly in the center/right aspect of the right knee; clicking noted during leg extension exercises (abs). One episode of mild knee swelling after first long run—resolved with ice. No current swelling, redness, heat, or pain at rest.  
• Aggravating factors: Running >2–3 miles, leg-extension core exercises.  
• Relieving factors: Rest, ice application, ibuprofen.  
• Associated symptoms: Single episode of tingling in right toes post-run; no giving way, locking, stiffness, limitation of range, or stair difficulty.  
• Previous joint issues: Bruised knee from ice-hockey fall several months ago; otherwise no chronic joint disease.  

Past Medical History:
• Refractive error (hyperopia) – treated with LASIK  
• Severe UTI in past (hospital evaluation, no stones)  
• No asthma, reflux, chronic GI, or systemic diseases reported  
Allergies: Not documented  
Medications/Supplements:  
- Ibuprofen 400 mg PRN (dose/route/frequency not fully documented)  
- Aleve (naproxen) PRN, dose/route/frequency not documented  
- Vitamin D daily (dose not documented)  
- Melatonin PRN for sleep  
- Xanax (alprazolam) PRN for severe insomnia, dose/frequency not documented  
- Occasional cannabis smoking  
Immunizations/hospitalizations: None reported beyond the above ER visit  

Physical Examination (tele-consult – patient-reported):
• Appearance: Alert, communicative, no acute distress  
• Right knee: Currently no visible swelling; able to fully flex and extend; no locking; no instability reported; no current tenderness described.  
• Left knee: Asymptomatic.  
• Gait: Walks normally; no pain on regular ambulation or stairs (by history).  
• Neurovascular: Normal colour and temperature of lower limbs; no ongoing numbness/tingling.  

Impression:
Likely overuse/over-training injury of the right knee (probable patellofemoral syndrome or soft-tissue strain); needs formal assessment to exclude meniscal or ligamentous pathology.

Management Plan:
• Continue intermittent ice therapy to right knee.  
• Relative rest: Reduce running mileage; stop any run that provokes pain.  
• Prescribed a stronger oral NSAID (specific drug/dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript) to be taken with food; instruct not to combine with ibuprofen.  
• Referral to physiotherapy for detailed knee examination, rehabilitation plan, and assessment of need for imaging.  
• Safety-net advice: Seek urgent medical review if knee develops persistent swelling, redness, heat, fever, or becomes locked/unable to move.  
• Option for in-clinic medical review if physiotherapy wait is prolonged.

Patient Summary:
Mary Jo, a 43-year-old marathon-trainee, developed progressive right knee pain and clicking after increasing her running distance two weeks ago. Examination suggests an overuse injury without red-flag findings. She was advised on rest, ice, prescribed a stronger NSAID, and referred to physiotherapy for comprehensive assessment.

Key Takeaways:
• Use ice frequently and limit running until pain-free.  
• Start the prescribed NSAID (with food) and stop all other OTC NSAIDs while using it.  
• Return promptly if knee becomes swollen, red, hot, or locks, or if systemic symptoms occur.

Next Steps:
• Attend physiotherapy appointment (referral sent).  
• Consider imaging (e.g., MRI) based on physio/clinical assessment findings.  
• Follow-up consult if no improvement or sooner if red-flag symptoms arise.
